newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot natgas prices ease for the weekend.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot natgas prices ease for the weekend.

text.p: U.S. spot gas prices slipped a couple of cents Friday in thin trade, pressured by forecasts for much milder Midwest and Northeast weekend weather and prospects most shut in gas from Hurricane Danny will be back.

"There's probably more than two billion cubic feet per day off the market, but everyone knows it's a short-term loss and the (hot) weather falls off dramatically over the weekend," said one Midwest trader, referring to a series of reports of production cuts on major U.S. Gulf pipeline systems.
On the Louisiana Gulf Coast, weekend prices fell two to three cents to the low-$2.20s per mmBtu, with gas at Henry Hub quoted in the mid-$2.20s after early reports of trades at $2.30 or better.
Danny was upgraded to a hurricane last night when sustained winds exceeded 74 mph.

At 1100 EDT, the storm was located at latitude 29.7 north, longitude 89.2 west, or about 55 miles east-southeast of New Orleans, moving northeast at about five mph with maximum sustained winds of 75 mph.
Danny was on track to make landfall in the next 24 hours somewhere along the Mississippi/Alabama coast.
In south Texas, prices dipped a few cents to about the $2.20 area, still well-above the July index of $2.06.
In the Permian Basin market, prices mostly were talked in the low-teens, off six cents, while southern California border stumbled almost a dime to the low-$2.20s.
In the Midwest, weekend prices were three cents lower at $2.09-2.14. Chicago city-gate gas also was quoted a few cents weaker in the high-$2.20s.
In the East, swing gas at the New York city gate was pegged about a nickel lower in the mid-$2.50s though some deals were reportedly done as low as $2.50.
The following pipelines reported production cuts Thursday and Friday because of Hurricane Danny:
- Columbia - 270 mmcfd
- ANR - 125-150 mmcfd
- Transco - 100 mmcfd
- Tennessee - 600 mmcfd
- Trunkline - 200 mmcfd
- Texas Eastern - 200-300 mmcfd
- Stingray - 71 mmcfd
Total Reported - 1,691 mmcfd

In addition, NGC's Venice gas processing plant was shut this morning due to high water from the storm. The plant, which typically receives about 750 mmcfd of offshore gas production, was expected back in service in two days.
((--J Silha, New York Power Desk 212-859-1624))
